Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Bot authors asked for three things:

> As a bot author, I don't want my bot to end up in every open room. I want to
> choose the rooms it joins.

> As a bot author whose bot serves everyone, I don't want to add it to each
> open room by hand.

> As a bot author, I want to know when my bot lands in a new room, so it can
> say hello.

So bots no longer join open rooms by default. People still do.

The bot form (new and edit) gets a new switch:

- "Add to all open rooms" (off by default)

When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room that appears later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships.

Whenever a bot is added to a room—automatically or by a person—its webhook receives a `joined` event, exactly once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/42-Xy3abc9defGh/messages" }
}
```

Direct conversations never trigger `joined`. The bot may reply to `joined` the same way as to `mention`: a `200` text or HTML reply is posted into that room as the bot's message.

# Chat bots

Bots are chat members that post messages over HTTP. They're aimed at shell scripts and CI jobs:
a deploy script can announce that it finished, a test run can post its summary.

## Model

- `Bot` (`bots` table) holds the bot's **code**, the credential that authenticates its requests, and its
  **creator** (the person who set it up).
- Each bot has its own `User` (`bots.user_id`, one-to-one). That user carries the bot's name and avatar and is what
  messages, memberships and notifications point at. So a bot is an ordinary member as far as the rest of the app is
  concerned: it's named and avatared like anyone, shows as the author of its messages, joins open rooms when it's
  created, can be granted closed rooms like anyone, and triggers push notifications the same way.
- The bot's user has no email address and a random password nobody knows. Bots never sign in, but the users table
  requires a password digest.
- Deleting a bot (`User#deactivate`, which the bot's delete button and the account members list both use) deactivates
  its user, the same as for people, and destroys the `Bot` row. That removes the code, so the bot can't post, but its
  past messages stay attributed to it.
- Bots are listed as members in the account's people list, the room member pickers and direct-message pickers, as
  people are. Removing a bot from the people list deactivates it, the same as deleting it on `/bots`. Changing a bot's
  role there has no effect, since bots never sign in.

Permissions reuse `User#can_administer?(record)`, which already lets a record's creator or an administrator manage it.
Any member can create bots. The list shows your own bots, or every bot for administrators.

## Web UI

- `/account/edit` has a bot icon link ("Set up chat bots") for every member, not only administrators.
- `/bots` lists the bots (no pagination). Each item shows the name, the creator (for administrators), an edit link
  ("Edit <name>"), and a read-only "Bot code" field with a copy button. The page is marked `turbo-cache-control: no-cache`
  so Turbo doesn't keep codes in its page cache.
- `/bots/new` and `/bots/:id/edit` share one form: avatar (optional), name ("Name the bot", required), webhook URL
  (optional, "Webhook URL", see [Webhooks](#webhooks)), "Save changes".
  The edit page adds "Delete this chat bot", which asks for confirmation with Turbo's `data-turbo-confirm`
  (the native `confirm()`).
- Forms that fail validation re-render with status 422.
- An empty file field doesn't clear the current avatar. The controller drops blank `avatar` params.

## HTTP API

```
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

Route: `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` (`bot_messages_path`), handled by `Bots::MessagesController`.

| Situation                                                     | Status                       |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| Message created                                               | `201 Created`, `Location: /messages/:id` |
| Unknown, deleted or banned bot code                           | `401 Unauthorized`           |
| Room doesn't exist, or the bot isn't a member of it           | `404 Not Found`              |
| Empty or whitespace-only body and no attachment               | `422 Unprocessable Content`  |

Checks run in that order, so an unknown code gets 401 whatever the room is. A response never includes the code.

Request bodies:

- **Any content type is taken as plain text.** The raw body is the message, with no JSON envelope and no field names.
  A body such as `100% done`, `a=b&c=d` or `{not json` is posted as written. Rails doesn't parse it (see below).
- The text is trimmed, and line breaks (`\r\n` or `\n`) are kept as line breaks.
- Invalid UTF-8 bytes",
  "output_tail": " URL or the code.
- **Empty, or made only of markup**: nothing is posted.

A reply goes into the room the mention came from, and only while the bot is still a member of it.

### Delivery rules

- Timeouts: 5 seconds to connect, 10 seconds to write and to read. A bot that needs longer should answer `204` and post
  later with `reply_to`.
- The address is checked with `RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard`, the same as link unfurling. `SECURITY.md` treats
  anything a non-administrator can reach through Campfire as in scope, and a member choosing the URL is exactly that.
  So loopback, private, link-local and unresolvable addresses are refused.
- The check happens when a webhook is called, not when the form is saved, since DNS can change. A bot running on
  `localhost` therefore can't receive webhooks, even in development.
- The connection goes to the address that was checked, so DNS can't change it in between.
- Redirects aren't followed.
- A reply is capped at 1 MB. The body is read in chunks, and an oversized reply is abandoned rather than buffered.
- Only a `200` reply's body is read. Other responses' bodies aren't.
- A reply's `charset` is honored. UTF-8 is assumed otherwise. Invalid bytes are replaced.
- There are no retries. A failed call is logged and dropped.

### Operating notes

- Webhook jobs run on the default queue, which push notifications use too. A slow bot holds a worker for up to about 10
  seconds per call. If that becomes a problem, give webhook jobs their own queue and workers in
  `config/resque-pool.yml`.
- Payloads aren't signed, so a receiver can't yet check that a request came from Campfire. Signing (an HMAC over the body
  with a per-bot secret, say) is the natural next step.
- The webhook URL is stored as-is, like the code. It's shown only to the bot's creator and to administrators, on the
  edit page, which is marked `turbo-cache-control: no-cache`. It can carry secrets in its query string, so treat it like
  the code.

## Security notes

- **The code is a credential.** It's 24 random base58 characters (`has_secure_token`), unique, and stored as-is,
  because the list has to show it. Anyone who holds it can post as the bot, so:
  - It's only shown to the bot's creator and to administrators, on `/bots`. Edit and delete pages don't show it.
  - It travels in the URL path, which is why it's masked everywhere a path or URL gets recorded:
    - Request logs: `lib/rails_ext/request_filtered_path.rb` prepends to `ActionDispatch::Request#filtered_path`,
      and `BotCodeFilter` masks `/rooms/:id/<code>/messages`. Parameter logs mask `code` (`filter_parameter_logging.rb`).
    - Sentry: `config/initializers/sentry.rb` scrubs the request URL in `before_send`.
  - Deactivating a user, or banning one, stops its bots from authenticating (`Bot.authenticate` only accepts active users).
- The endpoint is outside the session and CSRF machinery: `allow_unauthenticated_access`, `skip_forgery_protection`.
- Rails' parameter parsing is skipped for the body (`Bots::MessagesController#process_action`). Otherwise Rails parses
  form bodies (`100% done` is an invalid form, so it gets a 400) and JSON bodies (malformed JSON gets a 400). Multipart
  requests are still parsed, for the attachment.
- Bot text is HTML-escaped before it's stored, so bots can't inject markup into other people's pages.
- Webhook payloads carry the code in `room.reply_to`, which is how a bot replies, so a webhook's receiver holds the
  credential. The webhook's own log lines name the bot by id, never its code or URL. SQL debug logs still show row values
  (see below).
- Webhook URLs must be `http` or `https`, and are subject to the same private-address check as link unfurling (see
  [Webhooks](#webhooks)).

## Known limits and follow-ups

- The code isn't encrypted at rest. The app doesn't configure Active Record encryption keys, and the code has to be
  shown on the list. Adding encryption would mean adding keys to deployments, and `find_by(code:)` would need
  deterministic encryption.
- There's no way to rotate a code yet. Deleting and recreating the bot is the workaround. A "Regenerate code" action
  is the natural next step.
- No rate limiting on the bot endpoint. A leaked code can flood a room until its bot is deleted.
- SQL debug logs show the literal values SQLite queries use, including bot codes and session tokens, so don't run
  production at `RAILS_LOG_LEVEL=debug`.
- Bot-authored messages don't show a "bot" badge. The author name is the only marker.
- Neither bot text nor attachments have a size limit, the same as people's messages. A very large body is read
  into memory in full.
- System tests need a chromedriver. They didn't run in the sandbox this was built in (it has no network to download
  one). The UI was checked with controller tests, and by driving a running server in headless Chromium over the DevTools
  protocol: the form, the composer's autocomplete, posting a mention, and the native `confirm()` on delete.

{ "returncode": 0, "output": "# Bots post into rooms over HTTP, authenticating with their code. Each bot acts through its own user, so its # messages, memberships and notifications work exactly as they do for people. The code is the bot's credential: # whoever holds it can post as the bot, so it's only shown to the bot's creator and to administrators. # # A bot may also have a webhook URL. When a message mentions the bot, Bot::Webhook calls that URL. class Bot < ApplicationRecord has_secure_token :code belongs_to :user, autosave: true belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user } normalizes :webhook_url, with: ->(url) { url.strip.presence } validates :name, presence: true validate :webhook_url_must_be_http_url, if: :webhook_url? delegate :name, to: :user, allow_nil: true scope :ordered, -> { joins(:user).order("LOWER(users.name)") } class << self # Only bots whose user is active can authenticate, so banning a user stops its bots at once. Deactivating a # user destroys its bot outright (see User#deactivate). def authenticate(code) joins(:user).merge(User.active).find_by(code: code) if code.present? end # Bot text is plain text, so it's escaped before being stored as rich text: markup in it is shown as written. # Line breaks are kept. def html_from_text(text) ERB::Util.html_escape(text.gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip).gsub("\n", "
") end # HTML from a bot is kept to the markup messages are shown with. Attachments are dropped, so a bot can't mention # people, which would ping them, the way a person can with the @-mention autocomplete. def html_from_html(html) fragment = ActionText::Content.new(html).fragment.replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) { nil } ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters.apply(ActionText::Content.new(fragment, canonicalize: false)).to_html end end def name=(name) bot_user.name = name end def avatar=(avatar) bot_user.avatar = avatar end private # Bots never sign in, so this password only satisfies the user's password digest. def bot_user user || build_user(password: SecureRandom.hex) end def webhook_url_must_be_http_url uri = URI.parse(webhook_url) rescue nil errors.add :webhook_url, "must be an http or https address" unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present? end end ----- require "net/http" require "restricted_http/private_network_guard" # Calls a bot's webhook when a message mentions the bot, and posts what the bot answers with: # # - 200 with text/plain or text/html: the body is posted into the room as the bot's message. # - 204, or any other status: nothing is posted. A bot that wants to reply later can post over the bot API, using the # reply_to path in the payload. # # Bot::WebhookJob runs this, so a slow or broken webhook never holds up the person who posted the message. class Bot::Webhook OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5 # seconds READ_TIMEOUT = 10 # seconds MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 1.megabyte REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ] # Raised while reading a reply that's too big, to abandon the rest of the response. class ReplyTooLarge < StandardError; end # Failures reaching a bot are expected, so they're logged rather than retried. Anything else is a bug and raises. DELIVERY_FAILURES = [ Timeout::Error, SocketError, SystemCallError, IOError, OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError, Net::ProtocolError, Net::HTTPBadResponse, Zlib::Error, RestrictedHTTP::Violation, Surfguard::Unresolvable ] attr_reader :bot, :message def initialize(bot, message) @bot, @message = bot, message end def deliver reply = fetch_reply post_reply(reply) if reply.present? && bot_in_room? rescue ReplyTooLarge, *DELIVERY_FAILURES => e Rails.logger.warn "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} produced no reply: #{e.class} #{e.message}" end private def url @url ||= URI.parse(bot.webhook_url) end # The address is checked and then pinned, so the connection goes to the address that was checked, even if DNS # changes in between. Redirects aren't followed, so a bot can't send us somewhere that wasn't checked. def fetch_reply ip = RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(url.host) Net::HTTP.start(url.host, url.port, ipaddr: ip, use_ssl: url.scheme == "https", open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT, write_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT) do |http| http.request(build_request) do |response| # Returning from inside the block means the body of anything but a 200 is never read. return reply_from(response) end end end def reply_from(response) return reply_html(response) if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK) Rails.logger.info "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} answered #{response.code}, so nothing is posted" unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPNoContent) nil end def build_request Net::HTTP::Post.new(url, "Content-Type" => "application/json").tap do |request| request.body = Bot::Webhook::Payload.new(bot, message).to_json end end def reply_html(response) unless REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES.include?(response.content_type&.downcase) Rails.logger.info "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} answered 200 with #{response.content_type.inspect}, so nothing is posted" return end text = decode(read_reply(response), response.type_params["charset"]) if response.content_type.downcase == "text/html" Bot.html_from_html(text) else Bot.html_from_text(text) end end def read_reply(response) body = +"" response.read_body do |chunk| body << chunk raise ReplyTooLarge if body.bytesize > MAX_REPLY_SIZE end body end # Falls back to UTF-8 when the reply names no charset, or one Ruby doesn't know. Invalid bytes are replaced. def decode(body, charset) encoding = Encoding.find(charset || "UTF-8") rescue Encoding::UTF_8 body.force_encoding(encoding).encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace) end # A bot that was removed from the room since the mention can't post into it, the same as over the bot API. def bot_in_room? bot.user.rooms.exists?(message.room_id) end def post_reply(html) # Only bot messages with visible text are posted. A reply of nothing but markup is left out. return unless ActionText::Content.new(html).to_plain_text.present? message.room.messages.create!(creator: bot.user, body: html).tap(&:broadcast_create) end end ----- # The JSON a bot's webhook receives when a message mentions it. Paths are relative: the bot knows its own Campfire # origin. The reply_to path is the bot's own posting URL for the room, so a bot can reply later over the bot API. class Bot::Webhook::Payload attr_reader :bot, :message delegate :room, to: :message def initialize(bot, message) @bot, @message = bot, message end def as_json(*) { event: "mention", author: { id: message.creator.id, name: message.creator.name }, room: { id: room.id, name: room_name, reply_to: routes.bot_messages_path(room_id: room.id, bot_code: bot.code) }, message: { id: message.id, body: { text: text, html: html }, link: routes.room_at_message_path(room_id: room.id, message_id: message.id) } } end private def routes Rails.application.routes.url_helpers end # Direct rooms have no name of their own, so they're named after the people in them, other than the bot. def room_name if room.direct? room.users.without(bot.user).pluck(:name).to_sentence.presence else room.name end end # The text the bot is being asked, without the bot's own mention: "@Deploy Bot restart it" reads "restart it". # Mentions of other people stay as "@Name". def text content = message.body.body.fragment.replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) do |node| ActionText::Attachable.from_node(node) == bot.user ? nil : node end ActionText::Content.new(content, canonicalize: false).to_plain_text.strip end def html message.body.to_s end end ----- # Calls the webhooks of the bots a message mentions. See Bot::Webhook. class Bot::WebhookJob < ApplicationJob # The message may be deleted before the job runs, in which case there's nothing to tell the bots. discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError def perform(message) message.mentioned_bots_with_webhooks.each do |bot| Bot::Webhook.new(bot, message).deliver end end end " }

# Lets bots post messages from scripts and CI jobs. The bot code in the path is the only credential, and the
# raw request body is the message: no JSON envelope, no field names. Multipart uploads are the one exception: their
# `attachment` file becomes the message, as it does when a person posts a file.
class Bots::MessagesController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  before_action :set_bot, :set_room, :ensure_content_present

  def create
    message = @room.messages.create_with_attachment!(message_attributes)
    message.broadcast_create

    head :created, location: message_path(message)
  end

  private
    # The body is the message, not parameters. Left alone, Rails would parse it as a form or JSON document
    # before any action runs, and a body such as "100% done" would be rejected with a 400. Multipart is the
    # exception, since its attachment has to be parsed.
    def process_action(*)
      request.request_parameters = {} unless multipart?
      super
    end

    def set_bot
      @bot = Bot.authenticate(params[:bot_code])
      head :unauthorized unless @bot
    end

    def set_room
      @room = @bot.user.rooms.find_by(id: params[:room_id])
      head :not_found unless @room
    end

    def ensure_content_present
      head :unprocessable_content if message_text.blank? && uploaded_attachment.nil?
    end

    def message_attributes
      { creator: @bot.user, body: (message_html if message_text.present?), attachment: uploaded_attachment }.compact
    end

    def message_html
      Bot.html_from_text(message_text)
    end

    # Like the web app, a message is either text or a file, so a multipart request carries no text.
    def message_text
      @message_text ||= (multipart? ? "" : request_text).gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip
    end

    def request_text
      request.raw_post.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8).scrub
    end

    def uploaded_attachment
      params[:attachment] if multipart? && params[:attachment].is_a?(ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile)
    end

    def multipart?
      request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"
    end
end

module Membership::Connectable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  CONNECTION_TTL = 60.seconds

  included do
    scope :connected,    -> { where(connected_at: CONNECTION_TTL.ago..) }
    scope :disconnected, -> { where(connected_at: [ nil, ...CONNECTION_TTL.ago ]) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def disconnect_all
      connected.update_all connected_at: nil, connections: 0, updated_at: Time.current
    end

    def connect(membership, connections)
      where(id: membership.id).update_all(connections: connections, connected_at: Time.current, unread_at: nil)
    end
  end

  def connected?
    connected_at? && connected_at >= CONNECTION_TTL.ago
  end

  def present
    self.class.connect(self, connected? ? connections + 1 : 1)
  end

  def connected
    increment_connections
    touch :connected_at
  end

  def disconnected
    decrement_connections
    update! connected_at: nil if connections < 1
  end

    increment_connections unless connected?
    touch :connected_at

    connected? ? increment!(:connections, touch: true) : update!(connections: 1)

  def new
    @room = Rooms::Direct.new
  end

  def create
    room = Rooms::Direct.find_or_create_for(selected_users)

    broadcast_create_room(room)
    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  def edit
  end

  private
    def selected_users
      User.where(id: selected_users_ids.including(Current.user.id))
    end

    def selected_users_ids
      params.fetch(:user_ids, [])
    end

    def broadcast_create_room(room)
      room.memberships.each do |membership|
        membership.broadcast_prepend_to membership.user, :rooms, target: :direct_rooms, partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/direct"
      end
    end

    # All users in a direct room can administer it. Only direct rooms, though: this
    # relaxation is why room_scope below has to keep every other type out of reach.
    def ensure_can_administer
      true
    end

    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.directs
    end
end
class Rooms::InvolvementsController < ApplicationController
  include RoomScoped

  def show
    @involvement = @membership.involvement
  end

  def update
    @membership.update! involvement: params[:involvement]

    broadcast_visibility_changes
    redirect_to room_involvement_url(@room)
  end

  private
    def broadcast_visibility_changes
      case
      when @room.direct?
        # Do nothing
      when @membership.involved_in_invisible?
        broadcast_remove_to @membership.user, :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ]
      when @membership.involvement_previously_was.inquiry.invisible?
        broadcast_prepend_to @membership.user, :rooms, target: :shared_rooms, partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/shared", locals: { room: @room }
      end
    end
end
class RoomsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ show destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ destroy ]
  before_action :remember_last_room_visited, only: :show

  def index
    redirect_to room_url(Current.user.rooms.last)
  end

  def show
    @messages = find_messages
  end

  def destroy
    @room.destroy

    broadcast_remove_room
    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_room
      if room = room_scope.find_by(id: params[:room_id] || params[:id])
        @room = room
      else
        redirect_to root_url, alert: "Room not found or inaccessible"
      end
    end

    # Subclasses narrow this to the room types they're allowed to act on, so that one
    # room namespace can't be used to reach another's rooms.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@room)
    end

    def ensure_permission_to_create_rooms
      if Current.account.settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators? && !Current.user.administrator?
        head :forbidden
      end
    end

    def find_messages
      messages = @room.messages.with_creator.with_attachment_details.with_boosts

      if show_first_message = messages.find_by(id: params[:message_id])
        @messages = messages.page_around(show_first_message)
      else
        @messages = messages.last_page
      end
    end

    def room_params
      params.require(:room).permit(:name)
    end

    def broadcast_remove_room
      broadcast_remove_to :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ]
    end
end

module Message::Mentionee
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  def mentionees
    room.users.where(id: mentioned_users.map(&:id))
  end

  # Bots mentioned in this message that are in its room, are active, and have a webhook. A bot's own messages mention
  # nothing for this purpose, since a bot's reply can mention another bot, and that would set off a loop.
  def mentioned_bots_with_webhooks
    return Bot.none if creator.bot

    Bot.joins(:user).merge(User.active).where(user: mentionees).where.not(webhook_url: nil)
  end

  # A check made when the message is created, so it doesn't look anything up: it only says whether the body has any
  # attachment that could be a mention.
  def may_mention_anyone?
    body.body&.fragment&.find_all(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name).present?
  end

  private
    def mentioned_users
      if body.body
        body.body.attachables.grep(User).uniq
      else
        []
      end
    end
end

module User::Bannable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  def ban
    transaction do
      create_bans_from_sessions
      apply_ban
      banned!
    end
  end

  def unban
    transaction do
      bans.delete_all
      active!
    end
  end

  def remove_banned_content_later
    RemoveBannedContentJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def remove_banned_content
    messages.each do |message|
      message.destroy
      message.broadcast_remove
    end
  end

  private
    def create_bans_from_sessions
      sessions.pluck(:ip_address).compact_blank.uniq.each do |ip|
        bans.create!(ip_address: ip)
      end
    end

    def apply_ban
      close_remote_connections
      sessions.delete_all
      remove_banned_content_later
    end
end
module User::Role
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    enum :role, %i[ member administrator ]
  end

  def can_administer?(record = nil)
    administrator? || self == record&.creator || record&.new_record?
  end
end

  end

    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", bot.reload.name
  end

    bot = create_bot(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: users(:kevin))

  end

  module Enqueuing
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    included do
      ##
      # :singleton-method:
      #
      # Defines if enqueueing this job from inside an Active Record transaction
      # automatically defers the enqueue to after the transaction commits.
      #
      # It can be set on a per job basis:
      #  - true forces the job to be deferred.
      #  - false forces the job to be queued immediately.
      class_attribute :enqueue_after_transaction_commit, instance_accessor: false, instance_predicate: false, default: false
    end

    # Includes the +perform_later+ method for job initialization.
    module ClassMethods
      # Push a job onto the queue. By default the arguments must be either String,
      # Integer, Float, NilClass, TrueClass, FalseClass, BigDecimal, Symbol, Date,
      # Time, DateTime, ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone, ActiveSupport::Duration,
  # Registers a block to be called after all the current transactions have been
  # committed.
  #
  # If there is no currently open transaction, the block is called immediately.
  #
  # If there are multiple nested transactions, the block is called after the outermost one
  # has been committed,
  #
  # If any of the currently open transactions is rolled back, the block is never called.
  #
  # If multiple transactions are open across multiple databases, the block will be invoked
  # if and once all of them have been committed. But note that nesting transactions across
  # two distinct databases is a sharding anti-pattern that comes with a world of hurts.
  def self.after_all_transactions_commit(&block)
    open_transactions = all_open_transactions

    if open_transactions.empty?
      yield
    elsif open_transactions.size == 1
      open_transactions.first.after_commit(&block)
    else
      count = open_transactions.size
      callback = -> do
        count -= 1
        block.call if count.zero?
      end
      open_transactions.each do |t|
        t.after_commit(&callback)
      end
      open_transactions = nil # rubocop:disable Lint/UselessAssignment avoid holding it in the closure
    end

steps.message:
The system clock is 2026-11-23, so a generated migration will sort after the bot migrations. Before writing code, here's the plan I've settled on, with the reasoning behind each decision:

- **Storage:** a new `bots.add_to_all_open_rooms` boolean (default false, not null) in a new migration. I won't edit the existing bot migrations.
- **Default joins stop:** `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` skips bot users. `Rooms::Open` grants new rooms only to people and to bots with the switch on.
- **Switch:** `Bot` joins every open room after save while the switch is on. The join is idempotent, so turning it on joins existing rooms and later rooms still get joined.
- **`joined` events:** `Room::Memberships#grant_to` gets the user IDs that were actually inserted (`insert_all` with `returning`). Each new bot membership in a non-direct room enqueues one `Bot::JoinedJob`, after commit. This is the single choke point for "added by anyone, by any path".
- **Webhook refactor:** `Bot::Webhook` takes a payload object (mention or joined) rather than a message, so the delivery and reply logic is shared.

I'll start with the migration.

Each bot acts through its own user, so its # messages, memberships and notifications work exactly as they do for people. The code is the bot's credential: # whoever holds it can post as the bot, so it's only shown to the bot's creator and to administrators. # # A bot may also have a webhook URL. When a message mentions the bot, or the bot is added to a room, Bot::Webhook calls # that URL. # # Bots join only the rooms they're added to, unless they're set to add_to_all_open_rooms. Then they're members of every # open room, including ones created later (see User.joining_open_rooms and Rooms::Open). class Bot < ApplicationRecord has_secure_token :code belongs_to :user, autosave: true belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user } normalizes :webhook_url, with: ->(url) { url.strip.presence } validates :name, presence: true validate :webhook_url_must_be_http_url, if: :webhook_url? after_save :join_open_rooms, if: :add_to_all_open_rooms? delegate :name, to: :user, allow_nil: true scope :ordered, -> { joins(:user).order("LOWER(users.name)") } scope :with_active_webhook, -> { joins(:user).merge(User.active).where.not(webhook_url: nil) } class << self # Only bots whose user is active can authenticate, so banning a user stops its bots at once.   def default_involvement

  # Tells each bot in user_ids that it has joined this room, through its webhook. Direct rooms are private

    bots = Bot.with_active_webhook.where(user_id: user_ids).to_a

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "ok
class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      granted = Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } },
        returning: %i[ user_id ])

      # Only the rows that were inserted come back, so a membership that already existed doesn't announce anything.
      room.notify_bots_joined granted.rows.flatten
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

steps.message: Next is the delivery class. I'm changing `Bot::Webhook` to take a payload (mention or joined) and to post replies into the payload's room. I'm rewriting the whole file, since I have its full original text from the earlier read.

cd /app && cp app/models/bot/webhook.rb /tmp/webhook_before.rb && cat > app/models/bot/webhook.rb <<'EOF'
require "net/http"
require "restricted_http/private_network_guard"

# Calls a bot's webhook with an event (a mention, or the bot joining a room), and posts what the bot answers with:
#
# - 200 with text/plain or text/html: the body is posted into the room the event is about, as the bot's message.
# - 204, or any other status: nothing is posted. A bot that wants to reply later can post over the bot API, using the
#   reply_to path in the payload.
#
# The payload is one of Bot::Webhook::Payload (a mention) or Bot::Webhook::JoinedPayload. Bot::WebhookJob and
# Bot::JoinedJob run this, so a slow or broken webhook never holds up the person who posted the message or added the bot.
class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5 # seconds
  READ_TIMEOUT = 10 # seconds
  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 1.megabyte
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  # Raised while reading a reply that's too big, to abandon the rest of the response.
  class ReplyTooLarge < StandardError; end

  # Failures reaching a bot are expected, so they're logged rather than retried. Anything else is a bug and raises.
  DELIVERY_FAILURES = [
    Timeout::Error, SocketError, SystemCallError, IOError, OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError,
    Net::ProtocolError, Net::HTTPBadResponse, Zlib::Error,
    RestrictedHTTP::Violation, Surfguard::Unresolvable
  ]

  attr_reader :bot, :payload

  delegate :room, to: :payload

  def initialize(bot, payload)
    @bot, @payload = bot, payload
  end

  def deliver
    reply = fetch_reply

    post_reply(reply) if reply.present? && bot_in_room?
  rescue ReplyTooLarge, *DELIVERY_FAILURES => e
    Rails.logger.warn "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} produced no reply: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
  end

  private
    def url
      @url ||= URI.parse(bot.webhook_url)
    end

    # The address is checked and then pinned, so the connection goes to the address that was checked, even if DNS
    # changes in between. Redirects aren't followed, so a bot can't send us somewhere that wasn't checked.
    def fetch_reply
      ip = RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(url.host)

      Net::HTTP.start(url.host, url.port, ipaddr: ip, use_ssl: url.scheme == "https",
          open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT, write_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT) do |http|
        http.request(build_request) do |response|
          # Returning from inside the block means the body of anything but a 200 is never read.
          return reply_from(response)
        end
      end
    end

    def reply_from(response)
      return reply_html(response) if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK)

      Rails.logger.info "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} answered #{response.code}, so nothing is posted" unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPNoContent)
      nil
    end

    def build_request
      Net::HTTP::Post.new(url, "Content-Type" => "application/json").tap do |request|
        request.body = payload.to_json
      end
    end

    def reply_html(response)
      unless REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES.include?(response.content_type&.downcase)
        Rails.logger.info "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} answered 200 with #{response.content_type.inspect}, so nothing is posted"
        return
      end

      text = decode(read_reply(response), response.type_params["charset"])

      if response.content_type.downcase == "text/html"
        Bot.html_from_html(text)
      else
        Bot.html_from_text(text)
      end
    end

    def read_reply(response)
      body = +""

      response.read_body do |chunk|
        body << chunk
        raise ReplyTooLarge if body.bytesize > MAX_REPLY_SIZE
      end

      body
    end

    # Falls back to UTF-8 when the reply names no charset, or one Ruby doesn't know. Invalid bytes are replaced.
    def decode(body, charset)
      encoding = Encoding.find(charset || "UTF-8") rescue Encoding::UTF_8

      body.force_encoding(encoding).encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace)
    end

    # A bot that was removed from the room since the event can't post into it, the same as over the bot API.
    def bot_in_room?
      bot.user.rooms.exists?(room.id)
    end

    def post_reply(html)
      # Only bot messages with visible text are posted. A reply of nothing but markup is left out.
      return unless ActionText::Content.new(html).to_plain_text.present?

      room.messages.create!(creator: bot.user, body: html).tap(&:broadcast_create)
    end
end
EOF

# The JSON a bot's webhook receives when the bot is added to a room, whether by a person or automatically. Direct
# rooms never produce one. Like the mention payload, paths are relative, and reply_to is the bot's own posting URL
# for the room.
class Bot::Webhook::JoinedPayload
  attr_reader :bot, :room

  def initialize(bot, room)
    @bot, @room = bot, room
  end

  def as_json(*)
    {
      event: "joined",
      room: { id: room.id, name: room.name, reply_to: routes.bot_messages_path(room_id: room.id, bot_code: bot.code) }
    }
  end

  private
    def routes
      Rails.application.routes.url_helpers
    end
end
EOF
cat > app/jobs/bot/joined_job.rb <<'EOF'
# Tells a bot that it has joined a room. See Bot::Webhook.
class Bot::JoinedJob < ApplicationJob
  # The bot or the room may be deleted before the job runs, in which case there's nothing to tell.
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(bot, room)
    # The bot may have left the room, been banned, or lost its webhook since it joined. Then it isn't told.
    return unless bot.webhook_url? && bot.user.active? && bot.user.rooms.exists?(room.id)

    Bot::Webhook.new(bot, Bot::Webhook::JoinedPayload.new(bot, room)).deliver
  end
end
EOF
cat > app/jobs/bot/webhook_job.rb <<'EOF'
# Calls the webhooks of the bots a message mentions. See Bot::Webhook.
class Bot::WebhookJob < ApplicationJob
  # The message may be deleted before the job runs, in which case there's nothing to tell the bots.
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(message)
    message.mentioned_bots_with_webhooks.each do |bot|
      Bot::Webhook.new(bot, Bot::Webhook::Payload.new(bot, message)).deliver
    end
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class Room::BotJoinedTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  WEBHOOK_URL = "https://bot.example.com/hook"

  setup do
    @bot = create_bot(name: "Deploy Bot", webhook_url: WEBHOOK_URL)
    @room = rooms(:designers)
  end

  test "a bot granted membership of a room is told it has joined, once, through its webhook" do
    assert_enqueued_with job: Bot::JoinedJob, args: [ @bot, @room ] do
      @room.memberships.grant_to @bot.user
    end
  end

  test "granting a membership the bot already has tells it nothing more" do
    @room.memberships.grant_to @bot.user

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::JoinedJob do
      @room.memberships.grant_to @bot.user
    end
  end

  test "a bot listed twice in one grant is told once" do
    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Bot::JoinedJob do
      @room.memberships.grant_to [ @bot.user, @bot.user ]
    end
  end

  test "a person adding a bot to a closed room tells the bot" do
    assert_enqueued_with job: Bot::JoinedJob, args: [ @bot, @room ] do
      @room.memberships.revise(granted: [ @bot.user ])
    end
  end

  test "creating a closed room with a bot in it tells the bot" do
    assert_enqueued_with job: Bot::JoinedJob, args: [ @bot, Room.last ] do
      Rooms::Closed.create_for({ name: "Bots only", creator: users(:david) }, users: [ @bot.user ])
    end
  end

  test "a bot that joins every open room, when a new open room is created, is told it has joined that room" do
    switched = create_bot(name: "Switched Bot", webhook_url: WEBHOOK_URL, add_to_all_open_rooms: true)

    assert_enqueued_with job: Bot::JoinedJob, args: [ switched, Room.last ] do
      Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Later", creator: users(:david))
    end
  end

  test "turning the switch on tells the bot it has joined each open room" do
    switched = create_bot(name: "Switched Bot", webhook_url: WEBHOOK_URL)

    assert_enqueued_jobs Rooms::Open.count, only: Bot::JoinedJob do
      switched.update! add_to_all_open_rooms: true
    end
  end

  test "saving a bot that's already in every open room tells it nothing" do
    switched = create_bot(name: "Switched Bot", webhook_url: WEBHOOK_URL, add_to_all_open_rooms: true)

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::JoinedJob do
      switched.update! name: "Renamed Bot"
    end
  end

  test "direct rooms never tell a bot it has joined" do
    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::JoinedJob do
      Rooms::Direct.find_or_create_for(users(:kevin, :david).push(@bot.user))
    end
  end

  test "bots without a webhook aren't told" do
    @bot.update! webhook_url: nil

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::JoinedJob do
      @room.memberships.grant_to @bot.user
    end
  end

  test "banned bots aren't told" do
    @bot.user.banned!

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::JoinedJob do
      @room.memberships.grant_to @bot.user
    end
  end

  test "people are never told, since only bots have webhooks" do
    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::JoinedJob do
      @room.memberships.grant_to users(:kevin)
    end
  end

  test "a grant that's rolled back tells no one" do
    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::JoinedJob do
      Room.transaction do
        @room.memberships.grant_to @bot.user
        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

# Tells a bot that it has joined a room. See Bot::Webhook.
class Bot::JoinedJob < ApplicationJob
  # The bot or the room may be deleted before the job runs, in which case there's nothing to tell.
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(bot, room)
    # The bot may have left the room, been banned, or lost its webhook since it joined. Then it isn't told.
    return unless bot.webhook_url? && bot.user.active? && bot.user.rooms.exists?(room.id)

    Bot::Webhook.new(bot, Bot::Webhook::JoinedPayload.new(bot, room)).deliver
  end
end

## Open rooms

People always join open rooms. Bots don't, unless they're set to. The "Add to all open rooms" switch on the bot form
(off by default) sets that:

- When it's on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every
  open room created later. Turning a closed room into an open one counts as creating one.
- Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships. It only stops the bot joining rooms from then on.
- The switch never gives a bot a closed room. Those are still granted by a person, in the room's member list, the same
  as for people.
- Saving a bot that's already in every open room adds nothing, and tells it nothing.
- When a bot is added to a room, by the switch or by a person, its webhook gets a `joined` event (see
  [Webhooks](#webhooks)). A bot is told once per room: one that's removed from a room and added back isn't told again.
  Which rooms a bot has been told about is kept in `bot_joined_rooms`.
- Direct conversations never produce a `joined` event, even though a bot can be in one.
- A join that happens while the bot has no webhook isn't announced, and doesn't count as being told. A bot given its
  webhook later doesn't hear about the rooms it's already in, but it is told the next time it joins one of them while
  it has a webhook.

steps.message:
The scan is clean. The work is complete and verified, so I'll finish with the submit command on its own.

Summary of what changed:

- **Default joins stopped.** Bot users no longer join open rooms automatically. People still do, and new open rooms (including closed rooms converted to open) grant only to people and to bots with the switch on.
- **Switch.** The bot form (new and edit) has an "Add to all open rooms" switch, off by default. It's a real checkbox inside the switch styling, with the visible label. Turning it on joins every existing open room, and later open rooms are joined too. Turning it off keeps memberships.
- **`joined` event.** It fires whenever a bot is added to a non-direct room, whether by the switch, by room creation or conversion, or by a person. The payload matches the spec. A 200 text or HTML reply is posted into the room, using the same reply path as `mention`. Delivery is queued after the membership commits, so a rolled-back grant sends nothing.
- **Exactly once per room.** A `bot_joined_rooms` table records each announcement, with a unique (bot, room) index, so a bot removed and re-added is not greeted again.
- **Refactor.** `Bot::Webhook` now takes a payload object (mention or joined) instead of a message, and existing callers were updated.
- **Docs.** `docs/bots.md` covers the switch, the joined event, the once-per-room rule, and the known gaps.

Verification:

- **Tests:** full suite 467 runs, 0 failures (baseline was 418; the 22 skips are the system tests, as before). Rubocop is clean across 276 files, and Brakeman reports 0 warnings.
- **Browser:** I drove headless Chromium against a running dev server. The switch renders with the right label, starts off, toggles on click, and saves. A closed room created with the bot ran the join job through the async adapter. A new open room produced exactly one join. Removing and re-adding the bot produced no second join.

Decisions and caveats:

- `Bot::Webhook.new` changed signature from `(bot, message)` to `(bot, payload)`. Any caller outside this repo would need updating.
- I read "exactly once per room" as permanent per room. If you want re-adds to be announced again, that's a small change in `Room#notify_bots_joined`.
- A join that happens while the bot has no webhook is not announced later.
- There is no `left` event yet.
- System tests didn't run (no chromedriver here).
- The bot files are untracked in git, so their diffs don't show up in `git diff`. Nothing is committed.
